checks.invariant: Every DB-row string from sbFetch (res.json(), src/data/rest.mjs:83) that reaches an innerHTML/outerHTML-bound template must go through esc() (src/domain/core.mjs:14) or come from a numeric, boolean, or code-constant producer. Every attribute interpolation must be quoted, and no URL, eval, or document.write sink may take row data.
checks.result: Holds. I listed every `${...}` interpolation in app.js and src/**/*.mjs: 351 do not start with a known escaper, and each was triaged. Every DB text value is wrapped in esc() or fmtLineName, which runs esc first and only adds   afterwards. The rest are lengths and counts, Number()-coerced sums (resumoFrota num(), fmtN), boolean chips with constant labels, SECTIONS/LOC_FILTERS constants, the year list from getPortariaAnos (integers), or query-string parts. esc covers & < > " ' and all attribute values are double- or single-quoted; data-row uses single quotes and esc encodes '. There is no href/src/action/srcdoc/javascript: interpolation and no eval, new Function or document.write. toast uses textContent. PostgREST error text (err.message, rest.mjs:80-81) is shown only through errorBox or the drop-error template, both escaped. The suggest dropdown, datalists, select options, tab labels (renderTabs) and the line banner (paintBanner/bannerEmpHTML) all escape.

checks.invariant: Two inputs are raw by contract: metaRows value `v` (src/ui/doc.mjs:36) and tableHTML bodyRows (doc.mjs:49). Every caller must pre-escape them, and any unescaped DB value must be type-constrained.
checks.result: Holds. All 16 metaRows call sites pass esc()'d text, situacaoHTML/boolChip markup, or numbers. Every bodyRows builder escapes its cells. The only DB values inserted without esc are 7 fmtDate(...) calls: blocos.mjs:132,139; estrutura-tarifas-portaria.mjs:181,187; quadro-empresas.mjs:100,294; frota-historico-itinerarios.mjs:124. Their columns are all Postgres `date` (docs/backup_schema.sql:41,56,74-82,91) and no migration changes those types (no ALTER COLUMN ... TYPE in supabase/migrations). PostgREST therefore returns YYYY-MM-DD, and fmtDate's regex output is digits and slashes only. Even an ISO-prefixed text value would be reduced to the captured digits. This is safe today but fragile; see hardening.

checks.invariant: Three things are checked. The PDF export re-parse (baixarPdf, app.js:981-999: pdfHTML() string, liveDoc.outerHTML, or modalBody.innerHTML assigned to temp.innerHTML) must not re-materialize markup from escaped text. The data-row JSON round-trip (app.js:541,594,1191; listas.mjs:42,68; municipios-localidades.mjs:613) must not create a gadget. Injected id/name attributes must not be able to clobber a value the code later trusts.
checks.result: Holds. pdfHTML() is built by the same escaping builders. The outerHTML/innerHTML fallback re-parses in the same context (a div inside body). No row data sits inside raw-text elements (style, script, xmp, iframe, noembed, noframes, plaintext, noscript) or inside foreign SVG/MathML content, so the serialize-and-reparse round trip leaves the text inert. JSON.parse only creates own properties; there is no recursive merge, and the parsed row only reaches selectLine/paintBanner (escaped) and enc()'d query values. Because no row data reaches an attribute name or an unquoted value, there is no markup path for id/name clobbering. stripIds/restoreIds (app.js:829-830) only touch ids written by the code.

checks.invariant: The browser policy that would stop script execution if markup injection existed.
checks.result: The CSP in vercel.json has script-src 'self' with no unsafe-inline or unsafe-eval, style-src-attr 'none', object-src 'none', base-uri 'self', form-action 'self' and img-src 'self' data:. index.html has a single external module script (index.html:385) and no inline scripts or handlers. This is defense-in-depth only: the decision above rests on escaping, so whether the deployed header matches vercel.json is not decisive for this unit.

checks.invariant: Run end to end in Chromium, serving the real portal with the production CSP and a PostgREST stub built from the repo fixtures. Every displayed text column carries a payload combining attribute-breakout, img/svg handlers, a </noscript> breakout, xmp/style raw-text elements and a javascript: href. The payload must render as inert text on every surface, including the PDF export container.
checks.result: 21 surfaces checked: the hero search dropdown, the line banner, and all 19 view variants from check_views (each with its PDF export container captured from a stubbed window.print). Results: injectedElementsTotal=0, xssFlagSurfaces=0, no CSP violations. The payload appeared as inert text on all 21 surfaces (3-39 occurrences per surface; PDF containers 2-38). External HTTP was aborted and WebSockets were mocked. Sandbox: no network, loopback only. Check 02 was an earlier run that failed on a harness selector error and is superseded by this one.

hardening: fmtDate and fmtTime (src/domain/core.mjs:12-13) return input that does not match their pattern verbatim, and 7 call sites put fmtDate(dbField) into HTML without esc(): src/ui/blocos.mjs:132 and :139; src/documentos/estrutura-tarifas-portaria.mjs:181 and :187; src/documentos/quadro-empresas.mjs:100 and :294; src/documentos/frota-historico-itinerarios.mjs:124. They are safe only because those columns are Postgres `date`. If any of them is retyped or re-imported as text, they become stored HTML injection, which check-01 reproduces. Fix: wrap each call in esc(fmtDate(...)), or have fmtDate and fmtTime return esc(String(d)) in the fallback branch. Regression test: tarifaRowHTML({data_criacao:'<b>'}) must not contain '<b>'.

metaRows `v` (src/ui/doc.mjs:36) and tableHTML `bodyRows` (doc.mjs:49) are raw by contract, and esc() is enforced only by convention. Two possible guards: a Semgrep rule in .semgrep that flags template interpolations of fmtDate(, fmtTime(, orDash( or r.<field> not wrapped in esc( inside src/ui and src/documentos; or a CSP require-trusted-types-for 'script' together with a single escaping policy, as defense-in-depth for the roughly 135 innerHTML sinks.
